transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because my body just feels completely drained. Like... even just walking from my car to the clinic today took everything I had. I work at a clinic too, and lately, just opening the EHR feels like it takes all my energy. I just don't have anything left in the tank.
Aside from feeling so exhausted, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless lately?

Yeah, I have. Once all my energy just dropped off, I started feeling really empty. And hopeless, honestly. Most days it's just this heavy feeling... like I've already ruined my future in healthcare before it's even really started.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been... about nine months now. Yeah, nine months. That's when this whole depressed, exhausted, guilty feeling really started. It basically kicked in right after I crashed. Like... I had this really high-energy period right before this, and then I just totally crashed. And it's been this way ever since.
During that high-energy period, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual to feel energized?

Yeah, that's exactly what happened. For a while back then, I'd only sleep maybe two or three hours a night, and I still felt totally wired the next day. 

But lately... it's completely different. Now I either wake up way before dawn feeling just sick with worry, or... I'll sleep half the day away and still feel completely exhausted when I finally get up.
About how long did that period of high energy and needing very little sleep last?
It was... well, the whole thing kind of built up over about two months. It started right after my clinic changed my responsibilities at work.
During that high-energy time, did you feel like your thoughts were racing or moving much faster than usual?

I don't... I don't really think so. I mean, I had a lot of physical energy, but I don't remember my thoughts moving super fast or anything like that. I just felt like I could stay awake and keep doing stuff without getting tired.
During that high-energy time, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive, such as spending excessive money or making reckless decisions?

No, not really. I mean... I didn't go out and spend a bunch of money or do anything crazy like that. I mostly just used all that extra energy to keep working at the clinic and, you know, get stuff done around the place. I don't think I made any reckless decisions or anything.
During that high-energy period, did you feel unusually confident in yourself, or feel like you had special abilities or importance beyond your usual self?

Yeah, I actually did. I... I really believed I understood patient care way better than the nurses and the managers at the clinic. Even though I'm just a support worker, I was convinced that if they would just listen to me, I could completely change the whole system. I felt like I knew exactly how to fix everything they were doing wrong.
Did your behavior during that high-energy period cause any serious problems for you at work?

Yeah, it did. It got to the point where I just... I couldn't finish my documentation safely or stay focused on my regular patient-support tasks. Employee health actually ended up pulling me from work because of it, and they sent me out for an emergency evaluation. I also had to stop preparing for my CNA certification. I was trying to study for it, but I just couldn't keep up with everything anymore.
